Differentiating the fixed filling gives dmu/dT=-M1/(T*M0). Differentiating the mean energy then yields (M2-M1^2/M0)/T^2 with the stated positive sign and per-state normalization.
The completed approximation M2/T^2 is T*(dS/dT)_mu, equivalently the open-system heat response dU-mu*dN. It is correctly distinguished from (dU/dT)_mu and retains the exact equilibrium state.
At half filling mu=M1=0. C=x^2*sech(x)^2 and x>=4/3 imply dC/dW<0 for every calibration temperature; the global identification proof does not rely on the optimizer.

The finite canonical reference sums choose(M,k)*choose(M,N-k)*exp(-W*k/T), holds the integer total particle number fixed, and computes W^2*Var(k)/(2*M*T^2).
